Forecast product UX vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume weather capability in the binary covers storefront language. Connect and iOS actually separate in-app forecast behavior from product-page copy:

  • Forecast data & radar rendering — your app fetches conditions, hourly timelines, and radar tiles. Controls what buyers see after install — not App Store language. AppLocale does not implement this.
  • Location permission & alert delivery — geolocation prompts, push payloads for severe-weather alerts, and in-app notification settings. Engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • In-app weather UI — temperature labels, wind rows, UV index, and radar legend text on your screens. Your listing may mention hourly forecast; implementing forecast logic is engineering, not listing copy.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of forecast features in the binary.

A working hourly-forecast experience in the binary and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Weather-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Weather-app listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe forecast apps — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Forecast vs radar vs alerts

US pages mix "Hourly forecast", "Daily outlook", "Live radar", and "Storm alerts" in one gallery. China storefront copy often separates 天气预报 (general forecast), 小时预报 (hourly timeline), 降水雷达 (radar map), and 天气预警 (alert push) — depending on which frame you show. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual feature set, not inventing radar or alert capabilities your app does not support.

Condition screens & Apple Weather parallels

Many indie weather apps market Apple Weather-style condition cards — temperature, feels-like, UV, wind rows. Chinese buyers expect concrete labels (体感温度, 紫外线, 风速) on screenshot overlays rather than English slogans ("Know before you go", "Plan your day") that hide what the screen actually shows.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need weather-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 天气, 天气预报, and 小时预报 each signal different intent from generic utility keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Hourly forecast" headlines on gallery frames — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

Common mistakes on weather zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming forecast UI localizes automatically — radar and hourly timeline shipped; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and screenshot caption lines still English
  • Reusing US radar badges verbatim — Latin "Live radar" or "Hourly forecast" badges on zh-Hans screenshots signal unfinished localization
  • Conflating weather with MapKit — map pin and directions marketing belongs on the MapKit guide, not forecast or precipitation-radar copy
  • Mixing up weather with Calendar — Add to Calendar event-save captions localized but hourly forecast story still English on subtitle and description
  • Expecting AppLocale to implement forecast APIs — data feeds, radar tiles, and alert routing are outside listing rewrite
  • Ignoring caption fields per localization — zh-Hans screenshot set uploaded but overlay text fields never saved; see Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese
